illustrations.visual_goal: Map six financial-foundation chapters into three connected stages, culminating in money and terms a company commitment can rely on.
illustrations.layout: Single stacked column on a tall 9:16 canvas, six chapter cards one per row, explanation lines nearly as large as the titles and wrapped onto short lines; Gemini's empty paper margins cropped by the driver so the lettering scales larger at phone width. Heading "UNDERSTAND". Stage label "Trace money and control": "Customers, lenders, investors" / "Customers pay for what they buy" / "Lenders must be repaid" / "Investors hope for a gain"; "Funding and control" / "Who receives money" / "and approves spending". Stage label "Interpret value and returns": "Valuation" / "Estimating what" / "a business is worth"; "Investor returns" / "Gains or losses" / "on invested money". Stage label "Confirm funding for the work": "Funding choices" / "Match the money" / "to the work"; "Cash flow" / "Money coming in" / "and going out". Teal arrows between cards; ochre banner "Know what can fund" / "a commitment to do the work".
illustrations.alt: Six chapters stacked in three stages. Trace money and control: Customers, lenders, investors (customers pay for what they buy, lenders must be repaid, investors hope for a gain) leads to Funding and control (who receives money and approves spending). Interpret value and returns: Valuation (estimating what a business is worth) leads to Investor returns (gains or losses on invested money). Confirm funding for the work: Funding choices (match the money to the work) leads to Cash flow (money coming in and going out). A final banner reads Know what can fund a commitment to do the work.
illustrations.caption: Six chapters in three stages, each linked below.
illustrations.aspect_ratio: 9:16 (Gemini canvas 768×1376), cropped to content with a 20-pixel paper margin
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough
illustrations.prompt:

It maps six chapters, their reading order and their shared purpose; it is not a business scene. Tall portrait 9:16 composition. Match the book's visual language: warm ivory paper, dark navy text, clean slightly organic ink outlines, pale muted teal cards, soft ochre highlights, restrained flat fills, extremely subtle paper texture.

LAYOUT, STRICT: a single vertical column. Every chapter card spans almost the full image width (side margins no wider than one twentieth of the image), one card per row, six rows in total, read top to bottom. Never place two cards side by side. The image will be shown on a narrow phone screen, so ALL lettering must be very large and the cards must fill the column with little empty space. Sizes: each card title is bold sans-serif with a cap height of about one fourteenth of the image width; each explanation line under a title is regular sans-serif at EXACTLY THE SAME SIZE as the title (only not bold), never smaller, so that the explanation lines are as tall as the title above them; the stage labels and the bottom banner use the title size. Stage label 1: "Trace money and control".

Exactly six cards; every title appears once; reproduce the supplied words with exact spelling and add no other words. Symbols must contain no digits, letters, currency signs or percent signs. illustrations.alt: Four chapters stacked in one column under the heading ALIGN. illustrations.visual_goal: Show six chapters in four connected moves: agree what the work is for (outcome thinking); choose and justify work (including the three AI investment questions); assess what delivery requires; revise when the expected money is late.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "COMMIT".
Exactly SEVEN chapter cards organized into FOUR clearly separated horizontal bands, stacked from top to bottom. This is a compact overview, not a tall poster.

First band label: "Agree what the work is for".
TWO chapter cards in ONE evenly spaced row across the band, left to right, with an arrow from the first to the second:
"Adopt outcome thinking" / "Pair a customer outcome with a business outcome"
"Have your numbers ready" / "Define, own and label the numbers investors read"
The first card carries a small simple line-drawn symbol of two small pyramids side by side, joined by a short horizontal line between them; the second card carries a small simple line-drawn symbol of a card with a hanging paper tag. Both symbols are in the same navy ink as the outlines, placed so they do not crowd the text. No other card in this band.

A centered downward arrow connects the first band to the second.
Second band label: "Choose and justify the work".
Three chapter cards in ONE evenly spaced row across the band, left to right, with an arrow between the first and second and between the second and third:
"Set priorities" / "Fit the cash and team time"
"Test revenue assumptions" / "Does the change bring sales?"
"Clarify AI strategy" / "Sell it, use it, or be replaced by it?"
The third card carries a small simple line-drawn symbol of a brain outline inside a microchip, in the same navy ink as the outlines, placed so it does not crowd the text.
Inside the second band, below the three cards, one small single-line key in plain lettering: "Artificial intelligence (AI): software that predicts or generates content from data".

A centered downward arrow connects the second band to the third.
Third band label: "Assess what delivery requires".
ONE single chapter card, centered in the band, with a two-line subtitle:
"Assess capability" / "What can the software and team support, and what would a transition cost?"
No other card in this band; leave the space either side of the single card empty.

A centered downward arrow connects the third band to the fourth.
Fourth band label: "Revise when the money is late".
ONE single chapter card, centered in the band, with a two-line subtitle:
"Manage funding delays" / "Put cash and commitments on a calendar; choose one fallback in time"
This card carries a small simple line-drawn symbol of a calendar page with a small hourglass beside it, in the same navy ink as the outlines, placed so it does not crowd the text. No other card in this band; leave the space either side of the single card empty.

An arrow from the fourth band reaches one gold bottom banner: "Fund feasible work and review the evidence".
Only the listed seven chapter cards; no extra or duplicated card; the AI key line is the only footnote. Do NOT include any card about cloud costs, resilience, hiring, roles, system changes, growth, acquisitions or separations. Do not number chapters.
illustrations.alt: Seven chapters in four moves under the heading COMMIT. First, agree what the work is for: adopt outcome thinking, pairing one customer outcome with one business outcome and the investor metric it feeds, then have your numbers ready: define, own and label the numbers investors read. Second, choose and justify the work: set priorities to fit cash and team time, test whether the change brings sales, then separate the three investment questions inside an AI strategy request (artificial intelligence is software that predicts or generates content from data): sell it, use it, or be replaced by it. Third, assess what delivery requires: find what the software and the team can support and what a transition would cost. Fourth, revise when the money is late: put cash and commitments on a calendar and choose one fallback in time. All lead to one outcome: fund feasible work and review the evidence.
illustrations.caption: One chapter agrees what the work is for and one holds the numbers ready; three establish what deserves money, one what delivery requires, one what changes when money is late.
illustrations.placement: immediately after the heading The Learning Path, before the existing linked chapter walkthrough

illustrations.visual_goal: Show the five chapters as three levels of deliberate change (the team, the systems, the company's boundary) that all fund the transition before counting the benefit.
illustrations.layout:
Heading: "SCALE". One stacked column, five cards, one per row, read top to bottom, explanation lines at title size.
Group label 1: "Change the team".
"Scale the team up" / "Headcount is not capacity" / "Trace the work before hiring" (org chart with magnifying glass); short solid teal arrow down to
"Scale the team down" / "Decide what work stops," / "then who leaves" (list with one row crossed out); second short solid teal arrow down to
"Scale the team with AI" / "Test a capacity claim" / "with the same evidence" (person outline beside a small microchip).
Fine ochre rule.
Group label 2: "Change the systems".
"Plan for growth" / "Choose which system change" / "and how to fund it" (stack of blocks with one being swapped).
Fine ochre rule.
Group label 3: "Change the company's boundary".
"Plan acquisitions and separations" / "Account for the extra work" / "a new boundary adds" (dotted boundary around buildings).
Short teal arrow into the ochre banner on three lines: "Change size deliberately," / "fund the transition," / "keep the customer promise". No rail, bracket or connector between groups; the two arrows inside group one (cards 1-2 and 2-3) are the only inter-card connectors.
illustrations.alt: Five chapters in three groups under the heading SCALE. Group one, change the team: scale the team up only after tracing the work, because headcount is not capacity; scale the team down by deciding what work stops before deciding who leaves; and scale the team with AI by testing a capacity claim with the same evidence as headcount. Group two, change the systems: plan for growth by choosing which system change to make and how to fund it. Group three, change the company’s boundary: plan acquisitions and separations by accounting for the extra work a new boundary adds. A final banner reads change size deliberately, fund the transition, keep the customer promise.
illustrations.caption: Three chapters change the team, one the systems, one the company’s boundary; all fund the transition before counting the benefit.
